title: Hierarchy of Courts in India
description: The Indian judiciary follows a single integrated hierarchical system with the Supreme Court at the apex.

levels.name: Supreme Court of India
levels.jurisdiction: Appellate jurisdiction over all High Courts; original jurisdiction for fundamental rights (Art 32); advisory jurisdiction (Art 143); writ jurisdiction
levels.appointment: President of India on recommendation of Collegium
levels.appealsFrom: High Courts, tribunals, and special courts
levels.constitution: Art 124-147 of the Constitution of India
levels.head: Chief Justice of India
levels.notes: Highest court of appeal. Decisions binding on all courts in India (Art 141). Law declared by Supreme Court is the law of the land.

levels.name: High Courts
levels.location: One in each state/UT — 25 High Courts in total
levels.jurisdiction: Appellate jurisdiction over District Courts; original jurisdiction for fundamental rights (Art 226); writ jurisdiction; supervises subordinate courts
levels.appointment: President of India on recommendation of Collegium (CJI + Governor + Chief Justice of High Court)
levels.appealsFrom: District Courts, Sessions Courts, tribunals within the state
levels.constitution: Art 214-231 of the Constitution of India
levels.head: Chief Justice of the High Court
levels.notes: Each High Court has jurisdiction over one or more states. Some states share a High Court (e.g., Punjab & Haryana). Can issue writs for a wider range than the Supreme Court.

levels.name: District & Sessions Courts
levels.location: Each district has a District Court
levels.jurisdiction: Original and appellate jurisdiction in civil (District Judge) and criminal (Sessions Judge) matters
levels.appointment: High Court, in consultation with Governor and State Public Service Commission
levels.notes: The District Judge is also the Sessions Judge. Hears appeals from Magistrates and Civil Judges.

levels.name: Civil Judges (Junior & Senior Division) / Judicial Magistrates (First & Second Class)
levels.location: Each district has multiple subordinate courts
levels.civilJurisdiction: Civil Judge Junior Division (up to Rs. 10 lakh); Civil Judge Senior Division (unlimited, varies by state)
levels.criminalJurisdiction: Judicial Magistrate Second Class (up to 1 year imprisonment); Judicial Magistrate First Class (up to 3 years); Chief Judicial Magistrate (up to 7 years)
levels.appealsFrom: Civil Judge decisions appeal to District Judge; Magistrate decisions appeal to Sessions Judge
levels.notes: The lowest tier of the judicial hierarchy. Handles the majority of trial-level cases.

levels.name: Specialized Tribunals
levels.jurisdiction: Specific subject matters — tax, service, company law, consumer disputes, armed forces, etc.
levels.examples: Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Debts Recovery Tribunal (DRT), Armed Forces Tribunal, National Green Tribunal, Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions (National/State/District)
levels.appealsFrom: Appeals from tribunals go to the High Court and/or Supreme Court depending on the statute
levels.notes: Tribunals have replaced courts for certain matters to provide faster, specialized justice. Most tribunals are subject to judicial review by High Courts under Art 226/227.
